lead: Greensboro homes deal with humid summers, heavy storms and many crawl spaces. Moisture builds slowly under the floor, while leaks and storms cause sudden damage above it.
risk: crawl space moisture, storm leaks and frozen pipes
why: Many Greensboro homes sit over crawl spaces rather than slabs or basements. In the Piedmont's humid summers, damp air and leaks from plumbing or AC ducts collect under the floor. Wood joists and subfloors absorb that moisture, and mold or rot can follow. Problems often show up first as a musty smell, soft spots or cupped hardwood floors.

Storms bring sudden water. Summer thunderstorms and the remains of tropical systems can drop several inches of rain, and creeks such as North Buffalo and South Buffalo rise fast. Older neighborhoods like Fisher Park and Irving Park have homes from the early 1900s with aging roofs and plumbing. Winter ice storms and cold snaps can also freeze pipes in crawl spaces.

Fisher Park, Irving Park, Sunset Hills
tips: Check the crawl space twice a year for standing water or damp insulation.
Ask about a vapor barrier or crawl space dehumidifier.
Keep gutters clean so roof water doesn't pool by the foundation.
Insulate crawl space pipes before winter.
areas: Calls come from Fisher Park, Irving Park, Sunset Hills, Lindley Park, Westerwood, Starmount, Adams Farm and Lake Jeanette, plus High Point, Jamestown and Summerfield.

faq.q: How do I know if my Greensboro crawl space has a moisture problem?
faq.a: Look for a musty smell in the house, cupped wood floors, sagging insulation under the floor, or standing water after rain. Moisture meters give a clear answer. Drying the crawl space and fixing the source, like drainage or a leak, stops rot and mold.
